title: SLO-weighted degradation sheath: per-tenant & per-model graduated trippoints with safe degraded-model parachute
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Implement a production-grade ‘degradation sheath’ that computes SLO-weighted trippoints per tenant and per model, escalates isolation in graduated stages, and automatically switches to safe degraded-model parachutes or proxying paths (not hard circuit cut) during overloads. The design should prioritize predictable customer SLOs, observability for root cause, and safe rejoin policies to avoid oscillation.

Background: We see recurrent cross-tenant noisy neighbors and bursty model-specific spikes that cause cascading latency violations. Existing coarse global circuits either under-react (late trips) or over-react (wide kill switches). This ticket builds a fine-grained, SLO-aware containment layer that: (1) evaluates per-entity health with an SLO-centric score, (2) derives graduated trip thresholds tied to business impact, and (3) performs staged mitigation with safe degraded-model or region failover fallbacks before full rejection.

Proposal overview:
- SLO-weighted health score: combine P95 latency gap (actual vs target) and error rate into a single score normalized to [0,1]. Weighting is configurable per-tenant (higher for contract customers).
- Sliding-window & burst tolerance: 5s micro-window + 5m smoothing window; use exponential decay to prefer recent regressions while keeping hysteresis for stability.
- Graduated trip stages (example):
  Stage 0: observation (score < 0.6) - no action.
  Stage 1: mild degradation (0.6 <= score < 0.8) - reduced concurrency and small sampling to degraded model (5-10%).
  Stage 2: elevated (0.8 <= score < 0.95) - route 30-50% to degraded model variant; enable KV-prefix caching aggressive mode; shed low-priority requests.
  Stage 3: critical (score >= 0.95) - failover to degraded model 80-100% or region proxy, apply narrow tenant throttles, and engage rate-limited reject with informative error payloads.
- Safe degraded-model parachute: degraded variants are explicitly validated during onboarding (quality floor) and paired with automatic telemetry to detect quality regressions. If degraded variant quality drops below configured thresholds, fallback to throttling instead of substitution.
- Rejoin/backoff policy: cooldown windows per-stage with randomized jitter and probe sampling (shadowed replays at low rate) to confirm recovery before reopening higher capacity. Reopen logic uses decayed scoring and a minimum sustained healthy interval.
- Multi-region coordination: use primary-region score, but allow aggressive local degradation before cross-region redirect. Only escalate to cross-region failover for critical stage and after capacity checks to avoid cascading global effects.
- Observability & transparency: expose per-tenant per-model score, stage, and decision reason in Console; augment traces with "degradation_reason" tags and surface time-series on Dashboards + Pager alerts for enterprise customers.

Implementation plan:
1) Data layer: implement health-score calculator library (runtime-go) with pluggable metrics (latency, error). (Spike: 2d)
2) Control plane: new lightweight policy controller service that computes stages and issues adapter commands to routers. (Impl: 5d)
3) Router integration: add adapter to apply connection-level rate limits, sampling to degraded variants, and region proxy decision hooks. (Impl: 4d)
4) Degraded-model registry: extend model catalog with "degraded_variant" metadata and quality thresholds. (Impl: 2d)
5) Observability: Console panels, logs, and tracing keys. (Impl: 3d)
6) E2E tests: chaos + spike simulations, canary rollout, and synthetic customer scenarios. (Impl: 3d)

Acceptance criteria:
- Feature flag toggle with canary rollout in staging and a manual gating plan for production.
- Automated tests that simulate tenant spike and show progression through stages and correct switch to degraded variants.
- Dashboard showing per-tenant score, stage transitions, and end-to-end latency impact.
- Safety checks: degraded variant quality gating, cooldown enforced, and circuit oscillation absent in 90% of replayed spike workloads.

Risk & trade-offs:
- Complexity: more moving parts (controller + router adapters) increases operational overhead. Mitigation: keep controller stateless and rely on real-time metrics store; roll out behind feature flag.
- Quality trade-off: degraded variants may reduce answer quality. Mitigation: require quality vetting and customer opt-in for substitution for enterprise customers.
- Cost: cross-region failover increases egress/compute. Mitigation: limit cross-region to critical stage with explicit budget guardrails.
